checked_sources: Independent free-face and square complex reconstruction on three graphs
correctness.rationale: For every finite connected triangle-free K2,3-free graph, any neighbor set of cardinality≥3 lies in a unique generating closed neighborhood: two centers would share at least three common neighbors. For pairs, the only non-unique centers are opposite corners of an embedded square. In descending cardinality, (F,F∪{v}) is an actual elementary free-face pair except for those four exceptional centered pairs per square. Its residual is exactly graph plus tetrahedral boundaries, with each square contributing two disk fillings of the same 4-loop, second disk nullhomotopic in the first-filled CW complex. The pair count is Σ_v(2^deg(v)−deg(v)−1)−4q. Rectangular grids give a contractible filled-square CW, hence q spheres. Independently checked C4, 3×3 grid, and 5×5 toroidal C5×C5: counts (squares,collapse pairs,residual faces) = (1,0,14),(4,15,45),(25,175,225). Finite checks corroborate the all-graph proof; no inference beyond hypotheses.
residual_risks: No assertion for triangles or K2,3; no canonical natural wedge choice.
